label: sec:mass-physical-face-intro
html:
Specialising the six-term algebraic mass functional to the calibrated substrate parameter q_0 \approx 1.1100 produces concrete numerical predictions for the elementary and composite hadron spectrum. The neutron–proton mass difference m_n - m_p arises from the single crossing-sign asymmetry between the proton and neutron trefoil-linked three-strand braids, supplemented by the H_4(q) alternating-channel Habiro residual. The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 with hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G supplies the common baryonic bulk scale, while the torus-knot family T(2, 2k+1) combined with Seifert-fibre volume ratios reproduces the strange meson mass ratios m_K/m_\pi and m_\phi/m_\pi.

Across the light nuclear chart (1 \le Z \le 20), the three-channel brane-tower binding evaluation and the seven-term q-integer mass formula express nuclear binding energies and \beta-decay Q-values as the real and imaginary components of a single invariant, the complex volume \mathfrak{V} = \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} + i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta.
